new_findings.summary: One failed run ends the unattended night: after its own dispatched run fails, the autopilot never dispatches again, while the panel keeps reporting Running / Active target and the queue chip says Active.
new_findings.repro: Plan Tonight > Schedule > Run unattended all night with an eligible target. The autopilot dispatches Scheduler / M42-TEST (Slew > Center > Expose); the run fails 35s later ('Center Target: Failed to center within 5.0" after 5 attempts'). From then on the executor stays Failed and NO run is ever dispatched, while the engine keeps ticking and choosing the same target - 'Chose M42-TEST (score 4.501) at 00:52:51Z (tick)', 4.496 at 00:53:51Z, 4.491 at 00:54:51Z, 4.486 at 00:55:51Z - and the panel reads 'Unattended Autopilot - Running - Active target M42-TEST' with the queue STATUS chip 'Active' while the status bar reads 'Failed' (shots/waveE-sequencing/weseqn1-stuck-autopilot.png). Reproduced three times (runs failing 20:51:26, ~21:07:30, 21:18:46; still Running/Active 8 minutes after the last). It recovers only when the winning target changes: moving the site so nothing was eligible and back made the next evaluation dispatch normally. Matches the mechanism Wave D's refuter documented and the D-fix left open - packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:120-131 maps only SequencerEvent_Completed to sequenceCompleted, so currentTargetId stays pinned to a run that is over; stop()/_handleNoEligibleTarget were hardened against that stale state, the dispatch path still trusts it.

new_findings.repro: Arm the autopilot so it dispatches its own plan, then press the square Stop in the Sequencer while it is slewing (done at 21:18:42). Result: toast 'Critical - Sequencer / Slew: Operation cancelled', red 'Error: Slew: Operation cancelled' on the target card, run state Failed, and Execution History records 'Scheduler / M42-TEST - Aug 13 21:18 - 4s - Failed' (shots/waveE-sequencing/wdseqn1-autopilot-run-stop-critical.png, weseqn6-history-stop-vs-failed.png). The hand-started run stopped at 20:47 is recorded 'New Sequence - 42s - Stopped (resumable)'. The differentiator is either plan ownership or the instruction in flight (a Slew/Center returns cancelled and is escalated to a run failure); either way pressing Stop yields Failed + Critical.

new_findings.summary: The autopilot's generated plan has no Unpark step, so every dispatch after a safing park fails instantly on 'Mount is parked'.
new_findings.repro: Let the safety layer park the mount (observed toast at 21:14: 'Safe the rig - CRITICAL: Astronomical dawn is approaching. Rig safed: mount parked.'), then let the armed autopilot dispatch. The run fails in 0s with 'Error: Slew: Mount is parked. Please unpark the mount before slewing.' (History row 'Scheduler / M42-TEST - 21:16 - 0s - Failed'). The generated plan is exactly Slew > Center > Expose with no Unpark, and nothing in the dispatch path unparks. Any safing that parks (dawn, weather-safe, manual park) therefore breaks every later dispatch; with WE-SEQ-N1 that is one failure from a dead night.

new_findings.summary: Some captures launch two concurrent ASTAP solves of the same frame — one hinted, one blind — so the single-flight gate covers only one of the two callers.
new_findings.repro: Snapshots at 00:41:27, 00:44:17 and 00:44:30 each logged 'Plate solving near RA:0.00°, Dec:0.00°' + 'Running ASTAP … -ra 0.000000 -spd 90.000000 -r 30.00' and then, 3.6–23 ms later, 'Blind plate solving:' + a second 'Running ASTAP … -z 2 -d … -wcs' on the same file in scratch dir -1. ASTAP solves this frame in 0.04 s, so a 4 ms gap rules out fallback-after-failure — two callers solve at once and one discards the position hint the other used. The third engine-initiated teardown, the dawn park, does not: evaluation.dart:404-421 fires parkForEndOfNight() on _isEndOfNight && _dispatchedSinceStart && !_parkedForEndOfNight, with no _ownsDispatchedRun check, and the real sink routes it to SafeRigService.safeTheRig(park: true), which PAUSES the running sequence (safe_rig_service.dart:28-30 sequencePaused, :256-258) before parking. /tmp/waveE-refute/autopilot_ownership_dawn_test.dart, same takeover state as the batch's own pins but one tick later (clock advanced from 23:00 local to noon): parkCount Expected <0> Actual <1>, calls=[dispatch-begin, dispatch-end, park], and the operator's manual run is cleared. refuted.wave: E — dryness check, adversarial verifier (collateral damage over the D-fix batch ba5d102f2..558eccac3)
refuted.claim: D-fix 16b0a5fe7 / 558eccac3, 'a stop is not an error': the new NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped keeps a stop informative instead of alarming — its own doc comment says 'An operator (or safety trigger) chose to stop: worth telling a phone, never worth an alarm.'
refuted.how: It does not tell the phone at all. SystemPushTransport._pushSpecFor puts sequenceStopped in the `return null` arm (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/notification/transports/system_push_transport.dart:189), the arm documented as 'categories the mobile push feed intentionally does NOT escalate'. SystemPushTransport is the SINGLE mobile-push producer (its own header comment), so the phone push is not de-escalated from critical to info — it is deleted. PROVEN AT RUNTIME with a throwaway probe (dart run, /tmp scratchpad, no repo edits): a sequencer event {category: sequencer, eventType: 'Stopped'} classifies to NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped and SystemPushTransport.send() delivers 0 pushes and still returns success; the same transport with the pre-batch category (sequenceFailed) delivers 1 push at PushNotificationPriority.critical. Blast radius is the unattended case, because 'Stopped' is not only the operator's button: native RecoveryAction::ParkAndAbort is what weather_unsafe, dome_shutter_not_open and dawn_approaching triggers fire (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/triggers/manager.rs:295-372); ParkAndAbort cancels node execution (executor/start.rs:3476), the root node returns NodeStatus::Cancelled, executor_state_for_result maps that to ExecutorState::Cancelled (executor/trigger_context.rs:578) and the bridge maps Cancelled to SequencerEvent::Stopped (bridge/src/api/sequencer/event_bridge.rs:196). So a dome-shutter or dawn abort that used to page the operator's phone with a critical 'Sequence failed' now pages nothing. Caveat kept honest: the weather case likely retains a backstop via the separate SafetyEvent::WeatherUnsafe (bridge/src/event/system.rs:7) which still maps to the critical weatherUnsafe category; the dome-shutter and dawn aborts, and a remote operator Stop issued from the phone, have no such backstop. The batch's own test cannot see this — packages/skotiq_core/test/services/notification/event_classifier_stop_vs_error_test.dart asserts only the classifier's output and the enum's isCritical/defaultSeverity, never what a transport delivers, even though its header names 'a critical-priority phone push' as the thing being fixed.

refuted.wave: E — dryness check, adversarial verifier (collateral damage over the D-fix batch ba5d102f2..558eccac3)
refuted.claim: D-fix 3eadc3879, 'armed-autopilot warning': AutopilotArmedRule is an additive, display-only pre-flight warning that tells a hand-started run the scheduler is engaged.
refuted.how: It is not display-only — it makes synchronous sequence validation construct the autopilot engine. The rule does ref.read(schedulerStatusProvider) (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/autopilot_rules.dart:33), and schedulerStatusProvider is a StateNotifierProvider whose body does ref.watch(schedulerEngineProvider) (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:142-146). Building schedulerEngineProvider reads appSettingsProvider, schedulerPersistedConfigProvider, clockProvider, activeProjectIdProvider, schedulerCandidateLoaderProvider and schedulerTriggerStreamProvider, constructs _ExecutorSequenceSink(ref) and installs several ref.listen subscriptions (scheduler_engine_providers.dart:116-200). The rule was registered into defaultRefAwareSequenceValidators (sequence_validation.dart:354), and that list is run by SequenceValidatorService.validateSync — the path documented as 'Safe to call from non-async UI paths', i.e. live editor validation — inside a bare `for` loop with NO try/catch (sequence_validation.dart:444-453, 456-476). So (a) the scheduler engine and its trigger subscription now come alive from the Sequencer editor even when the operator never opens Plan Tonight, and (b) any throw during that provider graph's construction escapes validation uncaught; on the pre-flight path that is the gate that decides whether a run may start. The structural coupling is proven by code; I could not reproduce a throw in the running app, so treat the start-blocking consequence as PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed. The batch's test (packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/autopilot_armed_rule_test.dart) overrides schedulerStatusProvider with a fake, so it exercises the rule while hiding exactly this dependency.

refuted.how: Both seams the batch gated call _sequenceSink.stopSequence(). The third engine-initiated teardown, the dawn park, does not: evaluation.dart:404-421 fires parkForEndOfNight() on _isEndOfNight && _dispatchedSinceStart && !_parkedForEndOfNight, with no _ownsDispatchedRun check, and the real sink routes it to SafeRigService.safeTheRig(park: true), which PAUSES the running sequence (safe_rig_service.dart:28-30 sequencePaused, :256-258) before parking. /tmp/waveE-refute/autopilot_ownership_dawn_test.dart, same takeover state as the batch's own pins but one tick later (clock advanced from 23:00 local to noon): parkCount Expected <0> Actual <1>, calls=[dispatch-begin, dispatch-end, park], and the operator's manual run is cleared. refuted.claim: D-fix 16b0a5fe7 / 558eccac3, 'a stop is not an error': the new NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped keeps a stop informative instead of alarming — its own doc comment says 'An operator (or safety trigger) chose to stop: worth telling a phone, never worth an alarm.'
refuted.how: It does not tell the phone at all. SystemPushTransport._pushSpecFor puts sequenceStopped in the `return null` arm (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/notification/transports/system_push_transport.dart:189), the arm documented as 'categories the mobile push feed intentionally does NOT escalate'. SystemPushTransport is the SINGLE mobile-push producer (its own header comment), so the phone push is not de-escalated from critical to info — it is deleted. PROVEN AT RUNTIME with a throwaway probe (dart run, /tmp scratchpad, no repo edits): a sequencer event {category: sequencer, eventType: 'Stopped'} classifies to NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped and SystemPushTransport.send() delivers 0 pushes and still returns success; the same transport with the pre-batch category (sequenceFailed) delivers 1 push at PushNotificationPriority.critical. Blast radius is the unattended case, because 'Stopped' is not only the operator's button: native RecoveryAction::ParkAndAbort is what weather_unsafe, dome_shutter_not_open and dawn_approaching triggers fire (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/triggers/manager.rs:295-372); ParkAndAbort cancels node execution (executor/start.rs:3476), the root node returns NodeStatus::Cancelled, executor_state_for_result maps that to ExecutorState::Cancelled (executor/trigger_context.rs:578) and the bridge maps Cancelled to SequencerEvent::Stopped (bridge/src/api/sequencer/event_bridge.rs:196). So a dome-shutter or dawn abort that used to page the operator's phone with a critical 'Sequence failed' now pages nothing. Caveat kept honest: the weather case likely retains a backstop via the separate SafetyEvent::WeatherUnsafe (bridge/src/event/system.rs:7) which still maps to the critical weatherUnsafe category; the dome-shutter and dawn aborts, and a remote operator Stop issued from the phone, have no such backstop. The batch's own test cannot see this — packages/skotiq_core/test/services/notification/event_classifier_stop_vs_error_test.dart asserts only the classifier's output and the enum's isCritical/defaultSeverity, never what a transport delivers, even though its header names 'a critical-priority phone push' as the thing being fixed.

refuted.claim: D-fix 3eadc3879, 'armed-autopilot warning': AutopilotArmedRule is an additive, display-only pre-flight warning that tells a hand-started run the scheduler is engaged.
refuted.how: It is not display-only — it makes synchronous sequence validation construct the autopilot engine. The rule does ref.read(schedulerStatusProvider) (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/autopilot_rules.dart:33), and schedulerStatusProvider is a StateNotifierProvider whose body does ref.watch(schedulerEngineProvider) (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart:142-146). Building schedulerEngineProvider reads appSettingsProvider, schedulerPersistedConfigProvider, clockProvider, activeProjectIdProvider, schedulerCandidateLoaderProvider and schedulerTriggerStreamProvider, constructs _ExecutorSequenceSink(ref) and installs several ref.listen subscriptions (scheduler_engine_providers.dart:116-200). The rule was registered into defaultRefAwareSequenceValidators (sequence_validation.dart:354), and that list is run by SequenceValidatorService.validateSync — the path documented as 'Safe to call from non-async UI paths', i.e. live editor validation — inside a bare `for` loop with NO try/catch (sequence_validation.dart:444-453, 456-476). So (a) the scheduler engine and its trigger subscription now come alive from the Sequencer editor even when the operator never opens Plan Tonight, and (b) any throw during that provider graph's construction escapes validation uncaught; on the pre-flight path that is the gate that decides whether a run may start. The structural coupling is proven by code; I could not reproduce a throw in the running app, so treat the start-blocking consequence as PLAUSIBLE, not confirmed. The batch's test (packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/autopilot_armed_rule_test.dart) overrides schedulerStatusProvider with a fake, so it exercises the rule while hiding exactly this dependency.

holds: Enum-insertion safety: NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped was inserted mid-enum (between sequenceFailed and sequencePaused), the classic index-shift hazard for persisted per-category settings. It holds — persistence is by `storageKey => name` and NotificationRoutingMatrix.toJson/fromJson key on the string, never the index (notification_categories.dart:81, 393-425). No operator's saved routing rules shift.

New-category fail-open on load: NotificationRoutingMatrix.ruleFor does `rules[category] ?? _defaultRuleFor(category)` (notification_categories.dart:137), and fromJson skips unknown keys for forward compatibility rather than throwing. An existing installation whose persisted matrix predates sequenceStopped gets the built-in default rule, not a silent drop. (The drop is in the transport, not the matrix — see refuted #1.)

Third-party transport switch with a swallowing default: checked in_app, discord, mqtt, email, telegram, webhook, pushover. InAppTransport routes by category.defaultSeverity and only its _isPositive helper has a `default:` (in_app_transport.dart:53-65), so a stop renders as showInfo — informational, not the red error banner the fix was aimed at. Discord's default only affects embed colour. No transport other than systemPush changes delivery for the new category.

Per-device push mute bypass: DevicePushPreferences.allows() switches on the storageKey with `default: return true` (skotiq_remote_protocol/lib/src/push/push_token_store.dart:67-84), so a phone that muted 'sequence failed' would no longer suppress a stop. Documented fail-open, and moot in practice because SystemPushTransport never enqueues the category at all.

Headless add-frame classification survives the new LiveStackingFrameRejected wrapper: StackingHandlers._classifyAddFrameFailure branches on error.toString().toLowerCase() (apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/stacking_handlers.dart:240-272), and LiveStackingFrameRejected.toString() returns the engine reason verbatim by design, so 422 frame_rejected / 404 frame_unreadable still classify correctly instead of collapsing to 500.

saveMaster's new hard refusal of non-.png paths does not break an automated caller: the only production call site is the Stop-then-save flow in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/stacking_panel.dart:287, which already normalises the extension; there is no headless route and no end-of-run auto-save that passes .fits.

Scheduler ownership id stability: ownsRun compares the executor's loaded plan id to the dispatched Sequence.id. SequenceExecutor._ensureSequencePersisted early-returns for automated owners (sequence_executor.dart:663-676: 'Autopilot, Smart Night and mosaic ... their trees stay recoverable from the run's stored snapshot'), so the autopilot's sequence is never re-saved under a new id mid-run. The ownership test cannot go permanently false and strand a run.

Ownership-oracle fallback is not a shipping regression: _ownsDispatchedRun falls back to the old `_dispatchedRunId == runId` belief for sinks that do not implement SchedulerRunOwnership (scheduler_engine.dart:256-261). I hypothesised the headless/appliance path would keep the pre-fix semantics — refuted: _ExecutorSequenceSink is the ONLY production implementation of SchedulerSequenceSink in the repo and it does implement the oracle. The fallback is reachable only from test doubles.

No ref-after-dispose from the new oracle: ownsRun does two ref.read calls, which the sink's own header comment warns are forbidden during provider teardown. It holds because SchedulerEngine.dispose() calls only releaseSequenceOwnership (which uses the cached notifier) and never stop(); stop() is operator-initiated while the container is alive (scheduler_engine.dart:307-336, scheduler_engine_providers.dart:238).

Integration-follows-accepted-frames is consistent across surfaces, not a new divergence: SequenceRunStats.recordFrame now credits integrationSecs only when accepted (sequence_stats_provider.dart:158-170), which MATCHES the pre-existing SessionNotifier.recordExposure, where a rejected frame already incremented completedExposures/rejectedExposures and skipped totalIntegrationSecs (session_provider.dart:335-362). The two 'session integration' numbers now agree instead of disagreeing.

Ungraded frames still count as integration: the call site passes `accepted: graded?.accepted ?? true` (sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:143-147), so a run with no save path and therefore no grader event does not read 0 s integrated — the pass-making-direction trap this change could have introduced is closed.

'Stopped' consumers outside notifications were checked for the same failed-vs-stopped split and are consistent: the headless command correlator already accepts both {'Stopped','SequenceStopped'} for sequencer.stop (apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/command_correlator.dart:84), and the new runWasStoppedByOperator/runErrorMessagesFor helpers are identity-in/identity-out for every non-stop status (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/run_status_presentation.dart:46-76).

Scope: D-fix batch = commits 3eadc3879..558eccac3 (8 fix commits, 164 files, +10275/-2029), adjudicated at ba5d102f2 and recorded at baddf35fd. Six highest-blast-radius changes picked: (1) NotificationCategory enum + classifier + system push transport, (2) SchedulerRunOwnership / autopilot run ownership + evaluation generation guard, (3) LiveStackingService rejection wrapper + saveMaster format refusal, (4) SequenceRunStats accepted-only integration, (5) AutopilotArmedRule registered into the pre-flight validator stack, (6) run_status_presentation stop-vs-error helpers.

No repo edits were made. Runtime proof for refuted #1 was run entirely under the session scratchpad: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-scdouglas-Documents-Skotiq2/224b7868-cbfc-40e1-8fb0-99c71d23f174/scratchpad/dry/stop_push.dart, with a generated .dart_tool/package_config.json (relative rootUris absolutised from packages/skotiq_core/.dart_tool/) so `dart run` resolves package:skotiq_core outside the repo tree. Output: "classified category: NotificationCategory.sequenceStopped / send success: true  pushes delivered: 0 / control (sequenceFailed) success: true pushes delivered now: 1 / push: sequenceFailed prio=critical". Reusable trick for any flutter-free core probe.

Suggested closers, smallest first: give sequenceStopped a _PushSpec in SystemPushTransport with PushNotificationPriority.normal (gated on notifySequenceCompleted or its own toggle) so the phone hears "Sequence stopped" without an alarm — that is what the enum's comment already promises; and add a delivery-level test (category in, PushNotification out) beside event_classifier_stop_vs_error_test.dart, since a classifier-only test cannot see this class of drop. For refuted #2, either make AutopilotArmedRule read a lightweight status snapshot that does not build schedulerEngineProvider, or wrap the refAware loop in a per-rule try/catch so a validator can never take down the start gate.

The batch is NOT dry: one confirmed shipping-behaviour regression (unattended abort no longer reaches the phone) and one plausible structural hazard, both inside the two changes the batch was proudest of.
